summary: Detail that opens beside the content and leaves it usable — pick a row, read it in the panel, pick the next. A labelled region in the page, not a dialog.
useWhen: the detail of a list item should sit beside the list, and the next item should be pickable without closing anything — runs, tickets, records
the user compares or works down a list, reading each item's detail in turn
the detail is read or lightly acted on, not a task that must be finished or cancelled

useInstead.when: the page behind must not be touched until the task is done — an edit form, a filter set that applies on confirm
useInstead.why: that is modal behaviour, and a Drawer says so: it traps focus and hides the page. A SidePanel leaves the page live

useInstead.when: the detail is the whole of what the user came for — a record they will spend minutes in
useInstead.why: a panel is a side view; a record with sections, tabs and history needs a URL and the full width

useInstead.when: a sentence or two about one field

sm.use: a summary: a few facts and an action — 22rem

lg.use: detail with its own sections, on wide screens — 40rem

title.note: required — it names the region and is where focus lands on open

requires: a `SidePanelLayout` with the content first and the panel second — DOM order is reading order, and the panel is the detail of what comes before it
guarantees: a `<section>` region named by its title, rendered in place — not portalled, not a dialog, and nothing on the page is hidden or made inert
opening focuses the title, so the panel is announced and reading starts at its top
changing what an open panel shows does not move focus — the list can be arrowed through with the panel open
Escape from inside closes it; Escape elsewhere on the page does not. A Toggletip, Menu or Select inside closes first
closing with focus inside returns focus to the last thing focused outside it — the row picked most recently
no focus trap: Tab walks out of the panel into the rest of the page
closed, it renders nothing, so it leaves no tab stops
below 768px (`overlayBelow`) it opens as a Drawer, because there is no room beside the content and a panel covering the list must be modal to say so
it sticks to `--ion-side-panel-top` while the page scrolls, and its body scrolls when the detail is taller than the screen
the content column has `min-width: 0`, so a wide Table beside the panel scrolls in its own container rather than pushing the panel off screen
notes: set `--ion-side-panel-top` on the app shell (any ancestor) to the height of a sticky app header, or the panel's top slides under it
the title's heading level is `headingLevel`, default 2 — set it to follow the page's own outline
`isOpen` and `onOpenChange` usually derive from the selected item: open while one is selected, and `onOpenChange(false)` clears the selection

antiPatterns.dont: <Drawer> for a record's detail beside the list it came from
antiPatterns.why: a Drawer blocks the list: picking the next row means closing, clicking, reopening, and a screen reader is told the list is gone

antiPatterns.dont: a SidePanel holding a form that must be saved or cancelled before anything else
antiPatterns.why: a live page beside an unsaved form lets the user wander off and lose it; that task wants to be modal

antiPatterns.dont: the panel before the content in the DOM, moved to the right with CSS
antiPatterns.do: content first, SidePanel second, inside SidePanelLayout
antiPatterns.why: reading and Tab order would reach the detail before the list it is the detail of

antiPatterns.dont: moving focus into the panel every time the selected row changes
antiPatterns.do: let the panel follow the selection; it focuses its title only when it opens
antiPatterns.why: focus jumping to the panel on each pick makes the list impossible to walk with the keyboard
